label: Interception realization in a transition history
definition: The existing action has an interception contribution to a Threat targeting its own bearer, is ongoing, and its history admits no edge of any process with that exact Threat. The bridge is an explicit conjunction with a transition restriction, not an opaque successful-action flag.
note: OPEN analyst realization interface. InterceptionCandidate alone provides action role and target identity but no process suppression. RealizesInterception adds a substantive restriction on histories. Projecting it back to the existing candidate is a transcription, not evidence of a physical mechanism. Ordinary candidate: an ongoing guardian episode excludes the flame's admitted path; counterexamples include deleting a record with the path intact and removing a threat to a different bearer. Effective realization in reality, the adequacy of the state model and continuous-time interpolation remain open. Counterfactual contrast of histories alone is not efficient productive causation; this relation supplies neither CausesIn at esse nor ActualEsseCausesSupportAt. No causal structural order law is assumed.
